number.why: The numerical triplet is correct for the published intention-to-treat 28-day mortality rate ratio, but unconditional SERVED_CONFIRMED is incorrect when scale is included. The served effect object identifies a RISK_RATIO and the outcome specifies OR; neither is the reported log-rank rate ratio. This is an estimand mismatch, not merely an arm-count provenance-label imprecision. Retain 0.85 (95% CI 0.76–0.94) only with the correct rate-ratio estimand.

quotes.span: Overall, 621 (31%) of the 2022 patients allocated tocilizumab and 729 (35%) of the 2094 patients allocated to usual care died within 28 days (rate ratio 0·85; 95% CI 0·76–0·94; p=0·0028).

For the primary outcome of 28-day mortality, the log-rank observed minus expected statistic and its variance were used to test the null hypothesis of equal survival curves (ie, the log-rank test) and to calculate the one-step estimate of the average mortality rate ratio.
RR=rate ratio for the outcomes of 28-day mortality, hospital discharge, and successful cessation of invasive mechanical ventilation, and risk ratio for other outcomes.
In accordance with the statistical analysis plan (version 2.1, ), an intention-to-treat comparison was done between patients who entered the randomised comparison of tocilizumab versus usual care.
Outcomes were assessed at 28 days after randomisation to tocilizumab versus usual care alone, with further analyses specified at 6 months. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality.

entry.why: The report establishes hospitalised adults with COVID-19, restricted to hypoxia and systemic inflammation, randomised to tocilizumab plus usual care versus usual care. This population satisfies the question. Entry allowed clinically suspected or laboratory-confirmed infection; the question does not require laboratory confirmation.

quotes.span: This report is limited to adult patients.

Patients admitted to hospital were eligible for the study if they had clinically suspected or laboratory confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and no medical history that might, in the opinion of the attending clinician, put the patient at substantial risk if they were to participate in the trial.

Those trial participants with hypoxia (oxygen saturation <92% on air or requiring oxygen therapy) and evidence of systemic inflammation (C-reactive protein ≥75 mg/L) were eligible for random assignment in a 1:1 ratio to usual standard of care alone versus usual standard of care plus tocilizumab at a dose of 400 mg–800 mg (depending on weight) given intravenously.

missed: The ruling acknowledges the rate-ratio versus risk-ratio/OR distinction but fails to apply it to its confirmation and canonical RISK_RATIO typing. The quoted statistical methods and table definition establish that this distinction changes the scale adjudication. No additional finding changes the entry ruling.
